prior_attempt.rejection: The first recursive builder correctly unified ordinary and concurrent autonomous images, but rejected a whole root whenever one nested child was not autarkic, could not retain nested live clusters in the outer solve, and emitted all solved root images before ordinary root entities.

invariant: Java does not choose an ordinary-composite renderer or a concurrent-composite renderer for the whole diagram. CucaDiagramSimplifierState constructs the current group tree, reverses it into deepest-first order, replaces every currently autarkic group with an image leaf, and repeats until a complete pass makes no replacement. Entity.isAutarkic defines ordinary state-group eligibility semantically: package groups are excluded; every link must have both endpoint parent containers inside the group's ancestor closure or both outside it; and every surviving leaf must have NORMAL EntityPosition. Synthetic CONCURRENT_STATE groups are always eligible. Crucially, a non-autarkic child does not make an autarkic parent ineligible. GroupMakerState.createGeneralImageBuilder gives DotData an InnerGroupHierarchy that filters only synthetic CONCURRENT_STATE children; an ordinary child that was not replaced remains a real nested Graphviz cluster inside the parent's image. Conversely, every child already replaced by the fixed point is now an ordinary image leaf with solved dimensions. StateDiagram.concurrentState leaves the first region's entities directly in the owning STATE group and creates each later region as a nested CONCURRENT_STATE group carrying the same separator. Deepest-first replacement therefore turns each later region into a STATE_CONCURRENT image before considering its owner. GroupMakerState lays out the owner's first-region graph, including live ordinary child clusters and solved child-image nodes, then appends each already-solved concurrent image in source order. ConcurrentStates composes those region images by summing heights for '--' or widths for '||' while taking the orthogonal maximum. InnerStateAutonom wraps the complete body with the owner's title, attributes, margins, and border; its resulting dimensions become one image node for the next enclosing solve. Groups still live after the fixed point remain nested clusters in the root Graphviz solve. At every solve level, ordinary entities, solved image nodes, and live clusters retain the SVEK creation/emission stream instead of being emitted in type-wide batches.
causal_divergence: Commit 3c670edb ports descendant-based autarky and recursively composes ordinary/concurrent image nodes, but its recursion has only one successful child representation: AutonomousComposite. build_autonomous_composite_node applies ? to every direct composite child, so a non-autarkic child aborts an otherwise autarkic parent instead of remaining a cluster in that parent's Graphviz image. render_non_autarkic_root_clusters is not a general root fixed-point renderer: it rejects every nested composite, so a root made non-autarkic by an outside-to-grandchild link falls through to the flat renderer. Finally, render_autonomous_composite emits every solved composite before emit_autonomous_scope_entities emits ordinary root entities, even though Java's outer graph stream may place a previously declared plain state before solved composite images. The rejected heldouts preserve all three failures: InternalGrand1427 must remain a cluster inside an autarkic ancestor image, the ExternalRoot1453 tree must remain nested in the outer solve, and PlainBeacon1301 must precede two solved root images. These are representation and traversal errors; geometry constants cannot correct them.
planned_change: Represent the bottom-up fixed point explicitly as either a solved autonomous image or a live ordinary cluster for each composite. Extend the per-scope Graphviz builder so one solve can contain ordinary leaf nodes, solved child-image nodes with their computed dimensions, and recursively nested live SVEK clusters with their own group endpoints and member ownership. An autarkic owner builds its first-region image from that mixed graph rather than requiring every child to be an image; later synthetic concurrent regions remain independently solved images and retain the existing axis composition. The root uses the same mixed graph, allowing live nested cluster trees and solved root images to coexist. Drive SVG emission from the solved scope/entity stream: emit a solved composite when its image-node id is visited, emit ordinary entities in the same order, and emit live cluster chrome and descendants according to the cluster traversal, instead of front-loading all autonomous composites. Reuse LayoutGraph's parent-aware add_svek_cluster/build_cluster_tree support and existing SVEK endpoint semantics. Do not flatten a rejected child, pre-render a live cluster as an image, add depth/count branches, key behavior to heldout labels, or tune the canvas to the three counterexamples.
